topic.name: Conditional Variance for Continuous Random Variables

question.text:
\begin{align} f(x,y) = \begin{cases} x+y, & 0 \leq x \leq 1, \: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \\[5pt] 0, & \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \quad f_Y(y) = \begin{cases} \dfrac12+y, & 0 \leq y \leq 1, \\[5pt] 0, & \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \end{align}

Let $X$ and $Y$ be continuous random variables. Their joint probability density function and the marginal probability density function of $Y$ are shown above. Find the conditional variance $\textrm{Var}\bigg[X \,\bigg|\, Y=\dfrac{1}{2} \bigg]$ given that the corresponding expected value is $\mu_{X|\frac{1}{2}}=\dfrac{7}{12}.$
question.explanation:
Recall that the conditional variance of $X$ given $Y=y$ is defined by

\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}\big[X \,|\, Y=y] &= \textrm{E}\big[(X - \mu_{X|y} \big)^2 \,|\, Y=y] \\[5pt] &= \textrm{E}\big[X^2 \,| \, Y=y \big] − \mu_{X|y}^2, \end{align*}

where

\[ \textrm{E}\big[X^2 \,| \, Y=y \big] = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} x^2 \, f_{X|Y}(x \,|\, y) \: \textrm{d}x. \]

Note that $\textrm E\big[ X \,|\, Y = y \big]$ is a function of $y.$

The conditional density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ can be computed as

\begin{align} f_{X|Y} (x \,|\, y) &= \dfrac{f(x,y)}{f_Y (y)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{x+y}{\dfrac{1}{2}+y} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2(x+y)}{1+2y}, \end{align}

where $0 \leq x \leq 1, \: 0 \leq y \leq 1.$ Outside this domain, we have $f_{X|Y} (x \,|\, y) = 0.$

Now, substituting $y=\dfrac{1}{2}$ into the expression for $f_{X|Y} (x \,|\, y),$ we get

\[ f_{X|Y} \bigg(x \,\bigg|\, \dfrac{1}{2}\bigg) = \dfrac{2\left(x+\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}{1+2 \cdot \dfrac{1}{2}} = \dfrac{2x+1}{2} = x+\dfrac{1}{2}. \]

Therefore, we obtain

\begin{align*} \require{cancel} \textrm{E}\bigg[X^2 \,\bigg|\, Y = \dfrac{1}{2}\bigg] &= \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} x^2 \, f_{X|Y} \bigg(x \,\bigg|\, \dfrac{1}{2}\bigg) \; \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} x^2 \left(x+\dfrac{1}{2}\right) \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} \left( x^3 + \dfrac{x^2}{2}\right) \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \left[\dfrac{x^4}{4}+\dfrac{x^3}{6}\right]_{0}^{1} \\[5pt] &= \left(\dfrac{1}{4}+\dfrac{1}{6}\right)-0 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{5}{12}. \end{align*}

Finally,

\begin{align*} \require{cancel} \textrm{Var}\bigg[X \,\bigg|\, Y = \dfrac{1}{2}\bigg] &= \textrm{E}\bigg[X^2 \,\bigg|\, Y = \dfrac{1}{2}\bigg] - \mu_{X|\frac{1}{2}}^2 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{5}{12} - \left(\dfrac{7}{12}\right)^2 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{5}{12} - \dfrac{49}{144} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{11}{144}. \end{align*}

example.title: Calculating a Conditional Variance Given Joint and Marginal Density Functions

question.text:
\begin{align} f(x,y) = \begin{cases} \dfrac 87 xy, & 0 \leq y \leq 1,\; y \leq x \leq 2 \\[5pt] 0, & \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \quad f_Y(y) = \begin{cases} \dfrac 47 y(4-y^2), & 0 \leq y \leq 1 \\[5pt] 0, & \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \end{align}

Let $X$ and $Y$ be continuous random variables. Their joint probability density function and the marginal probability density function of $Y$ are shown above. Find the conditional variance $\textrm{Var}\bigg[X \,\bigg|\, Y=\dfrac{1}{2} \bigg]$ given that the corresponding expected value is $\mu_{X|\frac{1}{2}}=\dfrac{7}{5}.$
question.explanation:
Recall that the conditional variance of $X$ given $Y=y$ is defined by

\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}\big[X \,|\, Y=y] &= \textrm{E}\big[(X - \mu_{X|y} \big)^2 \,|\, Y=y] \\[5pt] &= \textrm{E}\big[X^2 \,| \, Y=y \big] − \mu_{X|y}^2, \end{align*}

where

\[ \textrm{E}\big[X^2 \,| \, Y=y \big] = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} x^2 \, f_{X|Y}(x \,|\, y) \: \textrm{d}x. \]

Note that $\textrm E\big[ X \,|\, Y = y \big]$ is a function of $y.$

The conditional density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ can be computed as

\begin{align} f_{X|Y} (x \,|\, y) &= \dfrac{f(x,y)}{f_Y (y)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\dfrac 87 xy}{\dfrac 47y(4-y^2)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2x}{4-y^2}, \end{align}

where $0 \leq y \leq 1, \: y \leq x \leq 2.$ Outside this domain, we have $f_{X|Y} (x \,|\, y) = 0.$

Now, substituting $y=\dfrac{1}{2}$ into the expression for $f_{X|Y} (x \,|\, y),$ we get

\[ f_{X|Y} \bigg(x \,\bigg|\, \dfrac{1}{2}\bigg) = \dfrac{2x}{\left(4-\left(\dfrac 12\right)^2\right)} = \dfrac{2x}{\left(\dfrac{15}{4}\right)} = \dfrac{8}{15}x. \]

Therefore, we obtain

\begin{align*} \require{cancel} \textrm{E}\bigg[X^2 \,\bigg|\, Y = \dfrac{1}{2}\bigg] &= \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} x^2 \, f_{X|Y} \bigg(x \,\bigg|\, \dfrac{1}{2}\bigg) \; \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{1/2}^{2} x^2 \cdot \dfrac{8}{15}x \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{8}{15}\int_{1/2}^{2} x^3 \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{8}{15}\left[\dfrac{x^4}{4}\right]_{1/2}^{2} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{8}{15}\cdot\dfrac 14\big[x^4\big]_{1/2}^{2} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2}{15}\left(16 - \dfrac{1}{16}\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2}{15}\cdot \dfrac{255}{16} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{17}{8}\\[5pt] \end{align*}

Finally,

\begin{align*} \require{cancel} \textrm{Var}\bigg[X \,\bigg|\, Y = \dfrac{1}{2}\bigg] &= \textrm{E}\bigg[X^2 \,\bigg|\, Y = \dfrac{1}{2}\bigg] - \mu_{X|\frac{1}{2}}^2 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{17}{8} - \left(\dfrac{7}{5}\right)^2 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{17}{8} - \dfrac{49}{25} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{33}{200}. \end{align*}

example.title: Calculating a Conditional Variance Given Joint and Marginal Density Functions

question.text:
\[ f_{Y|X}(y \,|\, 3) = \begin{cases} \dfrac {5}{2y^{7/2}}, & \quad 1\leq y \\[3pt] 0, & \quad \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Let $X$ and $Y$ be continuous random variables. Find the conditional variance $\textrm{Var}\big[Y \,|\, X=3\big]$ given that the conditional probability density function $f_{Y|X}(y \,|\, 3)$ is shown above and the corresponding expected value is $\mu_{Y|3}=\dfrac 53.$
question.explanation:
Recall that the conditional variance of $Y$ given $X=x$ is defined by

\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}\big[Y \,|\, X=x] &= \textrm{E}\big[(Y - \mu_{Y|x} \big)^2 \,|\, X=x] \\[5pt] &= \textrm{E}\big[Y^2 \,| \, X=x \big] − \mu_{Y|x}^2, \end{align*}

where

\[ \textrm{E}\big[Y^2 \,| \, X=x \big] = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} y^2 \, f_{Y|X}(y \,|\, x) \: \textrm{d}y. \]

Therefore, we obtain

\begin{align*} \textrm{E}\big[Y^2 \,|\, X=3\big] &= \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} y^2 \, f_{Y|X} (y \,|\, 3) \; \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{1}^{\infty} y^2 \cdot \dfrac {5}{2y^{7/2}} \; \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{1}^{\infty} \dfrac5{2y^{3/2}} \; \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \left[ -5\dfrac1{\sqrt y}\right]_{1}^{\infty}\\[5pt] &= 5. \end{align*}

Finally,

\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}\big[Y \,|\, X=3\big] &= \textrm{E}\big[Y^2 \,|\, X=3\big] - \mu_{Y|3}^2 \\[5pt] &= 5 - \left(\dfrac 53\right)^2 \\[5pt] &= 5 - \dfrac{25}9 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{20}9. \end{align*}

example.title: Calculating a Conditional Variance Given a Conditional PDF Using Improper Integrals

question.text:
\begin{align} f(x,y) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{2(x+2y)}3, & 0 \leq x \leq 1, \: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \\[5pt] 0, & \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \qquad f_Y(y) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1+4y}3, & 0 \leq y \leq 1, \\[5pt] 0, & \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \end{align}

Let $X$ and $Y$ be continuous random variables. Their joint probability density function and the marginal probability density function of $Y$ are shown above. Find the conditional variance $\textrm{Var}\big[X \,\big|\, Y=1 \big]$ given that the corresponding expected value is $\mu_{X|1}=\dfrac{8}{15}.$
question.explanation:
Recall that the conditional variance of $X$ given $Y=y$ is defined by

\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}\big[X \,|\, Y=y] &= \textrm{E}\big[(X - \mu_{X|y} \big)^2 \,|\, Y=y] \\[5pt] &= \textrm{E}\big[X^2 \,| \, Y=y \big] − \mu_{X|y}^2, \end{align*}

where

\[ \textrm{E}\big[X^2 \,| \, Y=y \big] = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} x^2 \, f_{X|Y}(x \,|\, y) \: \textrm{d}x. \]

Note that $\textrm E\big[ X \,|\, Y = y \big]$ is a function of $y.$

The conditional density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ can be computed as

\begin{align} f_{X|Y} (x \,|\, y) &= \dfrac{f(x,y)}{f_Y (y)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{2(x+2y)}3\right)}{\left(\dfrac{1+4y}3\right)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2(x+2y)}{1+4y}, \end{align}

where $0 \leq x \leq 1, \: 0 \leq y \leq 1.$ Outside this domain, we have $f_{X|Y} (x \,|\, y) = 0.$

Now, substituting $y=1$ into the expression for $f_{X|Y} (x \,|\, y),$ we get

\[ f_{X|Y} \big(x \,\big|\, 1\big) = \dfrac{2(x+2\cdot 1)}{1+4\cdot 1} = \dfrac{2x+4}{5}. \]

Therefore, we obtain

\begin{align*} \require{cancel} \textrm{E}\big[X^2 \,\big|\, Y = 1\big] &= \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} x^2 \, f_{X|Y} \left(x \,|\, 1\right) \; \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} x^2 \left(\dfrac{2x+4}{5} \right) \; \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{5}\int_{0}^{1} \left( 2x^3 + 4x^2\right) \; \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \dfrac15\left[\dfrac{x^4}{2}+\dfrac{4x^3}3\right]_{0}^{1} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac15\left[\left(\dfrac{1}{2}+\dfrac43\right)-0\right] \\[5pt] &=\dfrac15\left[\dfrac{11}6\right] \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{11}{30}. \end{align*}

Finally,

\begin{align*} \require{cancel} \textrm{Var}\big[X \,\big|\, Y = 1\big] &= \textrm{E}\big[X^2 \,\big|\, Y = 1\big] - \mu_{X|1}^2 \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{11}{30} - \left( \dfrac{8}{15} \right)^2 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{37}{450}. \end{align*}

question.text:
\[ f_{Y|X}(y \,|\, 4) = \begin{cases} \dfrac {8}{3y^{11/3}}, & \quad 1\leq y \\[3pt] 0, & \quad \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Let $X$ and $Y$ be continuous random variables. Find the conditional variance $\textrm{Var}\big[Y \,|\, X=4\big]$ given that the conditional probability density function $f_{Y|X}(y \,|\, 4)$ is shown above and the corresponding expected value is $\mu_{Y|4}=\dfrac 85.$
question.explanation:
Recall that the conditional variance of $Y$ given $X=x$ is defined by

\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}\big[Y \,|\, X=x] &= \textrm{E}\big[(Y - \mu_{Y|x} \big)^2 \,|\, X=x] \\[5pt] &= \textrm{E}\big[Y^2 \,| \, X=x \big] − \mu_{Y|x}^2, \end{align*}

where

\[ \textrm{E}\big[Y^2 \,| \, X=x \big] = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} y^2 \, f_{Y|X}(y \,|\, x) \: \textrm{d}y. \]

Therefore, we obtain

\begin{align*} \textrm{E}\big[Y^2 \,|\, X=4\big] &= \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} y^2 \, f_{Y|X} (y \,|\, 4) \; \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{1}^{\infty} y^2 \cdot \dfrac {8}{3y^{11/3}} \; \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{1}^{\infty} \dfrac8{3y^{5/3}} \; \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{1}^{\infty} \dfrac8{3}y^{-5/3} \; \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \left[ \dfrac 83\cdot \left(-\dfrac 32\right)\cdot y^{-2/3}\right]_{1}^{\infty}\\[5pt] &= \left[ -\dfrac4{ y^{2/3}}\right]_{1}^{\infty}\\[5pt] &= 0-(-4)\\[5pt] &= 4. \end{align*}

Finally,

\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}\big[Y \,|\, X=4\big] &= \textrm{E}\big[Y^2 \,|\, X=4\big] - \mu_{Y|4}^2 \\[5pt] &= 4 - \left(\dfrac 85\right)^2 \\[5pt] &= 4 - \dfrac{64}{25} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{36}{25}. \end{align*}
